resolutions.start_name: Faramid field wellpad cluster (Faramid Development Lease, East Obaiyed)
resolutions.researcher_notes: Resolves the 08-10 ROUTE_PARTIAL. START anchor is now hard: Faramid is a named DEVELOPMENT LEASE (map code 94) inside the East Obaiyed concession on the EGPC/EGAS/GANOPE Egypt Concession Map (eug.petroleum.gov.eg), bbox 26.9497-27.0666 E / 30.9999-31.0997 N, ~50 km2; five graded wellpads sit inside the traced polygon on Esri imagery (evidence/faramid_lease_and_pads.geojson). The repo's earlier start guess (30.9659, 26.8891, '30 km NW of Meleiha') is ~13 km off and falls OUTSIDE the lease - superseded. END anchor: the 07-2026 rejection of 'Badr El Din' as a 159 km false match is WITHDRAWN. Egypt Oil & Gas reports Agiba 'extending another line from the Faramid field to Badr El Din Company to process 24 mcf/d'; 'Badr El Din Company' is BAPETCO, which per SPE/JPT and Capricorn still operates Obaiyed/BED/NEAG/AESW after Shell's 2021 sale to Cheiron. The processing point is therefore the BAPETCO OBAIYED GAS PLANT (OSM flare nodes 11276921280/81/82; 'Petrojet El Oubaid' node 6960778686), not the BED field 159 km away. Sheet capacity 25.00 MMcf/d matches the '24 mcf/d' in the same sentence. GEOMETRY: the line is drawn along the EXISTING Obaiyed export right-of-way (OSM way/545729460), a multi-lane graded pipeline corridor visible continuously in Esri imagery from the Faramid pads WNW to the plant; it passes 1.07 km from pad B. Length 36.9 km vs 38.0 km on the sheet (0.97). The straight-line alternative (pad -> plant, no corridor) is 35.2 km (0.93) and never departs more than ~2.4 km from this polyline, which is why 'low (within kilometres)' holds under either hypothesis. NOT VERIFIED: no separate Faramid-specific trench is distinguishable from the pre-existing trunk in the basemap, and OSM carries no Faramid line - the corridor is inferred from co-location plus standard shared-ROW practice, not observed as a distinct new scar. Route [ref] cites the OSM corridor way and the plant node; the lease polygon comes from the EUG concession map, which is cited in the notes rather than as a URL ref because it is a raster map sheet, not a per-pipeline page.
